sites.summary: Bessemer Campus Expansion Site is an EPA ACRES brownfield property at 1092 Shiloh Lane in Bessemer, Jefferson County, Alabama; ACRES ships no acreage figure for this record and no owner could be independently confirmed for this specific parcel. The site sits near Project Marvel, a large QTS Data Centers (Blackstone-owned) hyperscale campus in Bessemer reported at roughly 1,607 acres, 4.5 million square feet and 1,200 MW. sites.name: PADUCAH GASEOUS DIFFUSION PLANT (USDOE)
sites.summary: The Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant is a 739-acre federal Superfund site in Kevil, Kentucky, owned by the U.S. Department of Energy and currently on the Final NPL. On 2026-07-29 DOE announced a partnership with Brookfield, NextEra Energy, Big Rivers Electric, Jackson Purchase Energy Cooperative, and Paducah Power System to build a more than $100 billion AI and high-performance-computing data center campus on portions of the site, paired with new natural gas generation and battery storage built and owned by NextEra. The data campus is planned to reach 1.8 GW of utility capacity and over 1.2 GW of compute load by 2032, with construction targeted for completion by 2031; the Big Rivers/Jackson Purchase power service agreement for the project remains subject to approval by the Kentucky Public Service Commission, which had not been granted as of the announcement.

sites.name: TAR CREEK (OTTAWA COUNTY)
sites.summary:
Tar Creek is a former lead and zinc mining area in northern Ottawa County, Oklahoma, listed on the Superfund National Priorities List in September 1983. Oklahoma DEQ describes the site as about 40 square miles; cleanup so far has remediated about 4,800 acres and moved more than 7.1 million tons of mine waste to the Central Mill Repository, with work continuing in the Elm Creek and Beaver Creek watersheds.

EPA issued its seventh five-year review of the remedy in September 2025, and DEQ, EPA Region 6 and the Quapaw Nation held a public open house on the cleanup in Miami, Oklahoma, on March 5, 2026.

sites.name: SAVANNAH RIVER SITE (USDOE)
sites.summary: The Savannah River Site is a large federal Superfund site in Aiken, South Carolina, owned by the U.S. Department of Energy, placed on the NPL in 1989 and currently on the Final NPL, with site management and operations handled by Savannah River Nuclear Solutions, LLC. On 2026-07-20 the National Nuclear Security Administration selected Amentum to enter negotiations for a phased lease to build a roughly 1-gigawatt AI data center paired with about 2 gigawatts of on-site generation (natural gas initially, with a stated intent to transition toward advanced nuclear energy); NNSA's announcement explicitly states selection for negotiations does not constitute a final lease award, and as of the announcement no lease had been signed. Separately, on 2026-08-25 DOE's Office of Environmental Management authorized the fifth mega-size Saltstone Disposal Unit (SDU 10) at the site for operations, allowing it to begin receiving decontaminated salt solution as part of ongoing liquid waste cleanup.

sites.name: OAK RIDGE RESERVATION (USDOE)
sites.summary: Oak Ridge Reservation is a DOE facility of nearly 35,000 acres in and next to the city of Oak Ridge, Tennessee, under EPA Superfund cleanup. NRC staff recommended a construction permit for TVA's BWRX-300 reactor at the nearby Clinch River site in June 2026; no issued permit was confirmed in an agency or primary source as of 2026-09-29.

sites.name: PANTEX PLANT (USDOE)
sites.summary: Pantex Plant is an active DOE/NNSA nuclear weapons facility about 17 miles northeast of Amarillo in Carson County, Texas, and a federal-facility Superfund site added to the National Priorities List in 1994. EPA describes the site as about 16,000 acres, about 10,000 owned by DOE and about 6,000 leased from Texas Tech University. NNSA selected PanTeXas Deterrence, LLC as the plant's management and operating contractor in 2024, and DOE's Office of Enforcement notified that operator on 2026-07-29 of an investigation into the protection of a classified computer.

sites.name: FOX RIVER NRDA/PCB RELEASES
sites.summary: The Fox River site covers PCB-contaminated sediment in the Lower Fox River, which runs 39 miles from the Neenah and Menasha channels to Green Bay, and in the bay itself. Wisconsin DNR reports active cleanup finished in 2020, EPA certified completion in October 2022, and the site is now in long-term monitoring. The most recent dated milestone found is the January 2023 start of Wisconsin's state closure process; no developments after 2025-10-01 were found.
